correctness.rationale: A fixed simplex in the prism perfect-matching complex consists of rung-edge orbits and paired horizontal-edge orbits. Invariance plus matching condition makes these correspond exactly to matching faces of W(H), and every such invariant partial matching extends by adjoining all unused rungs; orbit barycenters therefore yield an actual PL homeomorphism, not just a chain identity. The subcomplex A formed by all rung closed stars has contractible nonempty finite intersections: any face compatible with each chosen rung is compatible with their union. Its nerve is a full simplex, so A is contractible even for an isolated vertex. Any horizontal face leaving an uncovered base vertex lies in A. Faces outside A are exactly entire perfect matchings of H, with dimension m-1 when n=2m, and all boundaries lie in A; this gives a relative free top chain group and K/A wedge of one sphere per perfect matching. Collapsing contractible A is a homotopy equivalence; the edge-order orientation action gives the integral signed permutation representation. For n odd no exceptional facets, hence contractible; zero-dimensional m=1 and b(H)=0 cases handled. Independently enumerated base perfect matching counts for P3,P4,C4,K4,K3,3 (0,1,2,3,6), agreeing with exception facet classification. This is independent finite support, not a proof for all H.

No claim for full prism perfect-matching complex or equivariant homotopy splitting.
